turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you got a sec? I need to vent about the DNS switchover yesterday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? I saw the incident page light up around 2 PM.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, that was me. I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was actually ready. I thought the warm-up would be faster.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ouch. So the traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. Every region went down — the outage lasted for hours. Customers in APAC, EU, US — all of them. I felt sick watching the dashboards.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's brutal. But hey, at least you know what not to do next time, right?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I've already written a postmortem. The fix is simple: I'll wait for the cluster health check before switching DNS. No more cowboy moves.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sounds reasonable. Health check passes, then flip. I'll hold you to it.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good news — the DNS switchover this morning went perfectly.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice! So you actually waited for the health check this time?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yep, I set a timer, watched the cluster report green for a full five minutes, then flipped the DNS. Traffic moved over without a hitch. Zero errors.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's the way. So we're all good now?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Mostly. But I also had a scare with the database migration last night.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What happened? You didn't migrate the schema without a backup again, did you?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I almost did — but no, I took a full snapshot before the migration. Good thing too, because the migration corrupted customer records. Addresses got scrambled, some orders linked to the wrong accounts.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yikes. But you had the snapshot, so you could roll back?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. The migration could always be rolled back — I restored in under ten minutes. No lasting damage. Lesson learned: never skip the backup.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Two close calls in one week. You're building a good habit of learning the hard way.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, I need to tell you something about the DNS fix. Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What do you mean? The health check wait worked — we had a clean switchover last time.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It worked because I was disciplined. But last night, I got paged at 3 AM for a different cluster, and I was so sleep-deprived I almost flipped DNS without checking the health status. I caught myself at the last second.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Whoa. So the manual wait is fragile — it depends on the human remembering.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about relying on my own vigilance. So I replaced the manual wait with automated health-check-gated DNS failover. The system now checks the cluster health continuously, and if the cluster is dead, traffic auto-routes away — no human in the loop.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a big upgrade. So even if you're half-asleep, the DNS won't point at a bad cluster?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Right. The old approach — waiting for the health check before switching — fell short because it only protected the initial switch. It didn't protect against future failures or human error. Now the gate is always on.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's the right call. You turned a one-time fix into a permanent safety net.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah. I just wish I'd done it after the first outage. But better late than never.
